A letter from my heart

To Tarun,
with love.

Some things are easier to write than to say. This is everything I never managed to put into words.

Before we knew each other

Two little lives, long before they crossed.

These are two little versions of us, from completely different times in our lives—before either of us knew the other existed. Somehow, years later, our paths crossed, and we became part of each other's lives.

Written from the heart

To the person I still love,

I really wanted to write this letter to you because I want you to understand just how much our relationship meant to me. I know a letter can't change what happened between us, undo my mistakes, or make the hurt disappear. But there are so many things I never properly said, and I don't want to leave them unsaid.

I want you to know how deeply I loved you, how much I valued the time we shared, how much the little moments meant to me, and how much I regret the things I did that hurt you.

This isn't me trying to pressure you into anything. It's simply me opening my heart and showing you everything I've been carrying inside.

I don't really know where to begin, because there are so many things I still carry inside me that I never managed to say properly.

I know things between us became complicated. We misunderstood each other, we argued, and sometimes the arguments became bigger than the love that was supposed to bring us back together. Especially when it came to politics. I hate how much those disagreements affected us. I hate that something outside of us became something that could hurt something so deeply personal between us.

I still love you.

I don't mean that because I'm afraid of being alone. I mean it because when I think about you, I still remember the person I fell in love with—not just the difficult moments, but all the little things that made you you.

I still remember the way you talked about your feelings growing. The way you said you wanted to please me, tease me, annoy me, and love me to an almost annoying degree. Those words stayed with me more than you probably realize.

And I remember all the little names I used to call you—my Brownie, my Teddy Bear, my Bubu. They were silly little names, but they belonged to us. Every time I called you one of them, there was so much affection behind it. I miss being able to call you those names. I miss that little world that existed between us where those names meant something only we truly understood.

And I remember how much you cared.

When we went away from each other before, you were hurt. You cried. You didn't simply act like I meant nothing to you. You worried about me. You asked about my treatment, my anxiety, whether I was sleeping, whether I was okay. Those things mattered to me because they showed me that somewhere inside you, my wellbeing mattered.

There is something else I want you to know. I have forgotten people and little things about myself before, and that has always scared me in ways I never really knew how to explain. But I don't want to forget you. I don't want the memories of you, the little things you said, the way you cared, or the moments we shared to disappear with time. Even if life changes and memories become harder to hold onto, I want the memory of you to remain something I protect and cherish.

I still remember the little things you used to tell me too—like how you would tell me to put my phone aside when I was going to sleep. It was such a simple thing, but looking back, I realize it was one of those quiet ways you cared about me. You wanted me to rest and take care of myself. I miss those little reminders more than I ever thought I would.

And I remember how I used to remind you to drink water too. It was such a small thing, but it was one of my little ways of caring about you and wanting you to take care of yourself.

I also remember that you wanted me to guide you with your studies. I used to ask you how much you had studied, what you had finished, and how you were doing with everything. Even now, I still find myself wanting to ask you those things—not because I want to control you, but because caring about your life and wanting to see you do well became such a natural part of loving you.

I still remember the little future thoughts we had too. You talking about wanting to go to Japan and wondering how I would even come with you because I had never properly shown you my face. Even wondering how I would handle eating non-veg there. They might sound like tiny things now, but those tiny conversations were pieces of a future we once imagined without even realizing how precious they were.

And there's something else I haven't really known how to say.

Since we broke up, I've lost around 5 kg. I know that might sound like just a number, but for me, it became a reflection of how badly I was struggling to cope with everything. I wasn't taking care of myself the way I should have been.

I'm not telling you this to make you feel guilty or responsible. I just want you to understand that losing us affected me deeply, even when I tried to act like I was okay.

I regret so many of the misunderstandings between us.

I regret the moments when I allowed arguments to become more important than understanding you. I regret the times I made you feel unheard or hurt. And I especially regret the way our political disagreements kept creating distance between us.

I also know I broke a lot of promises I made to you.

I remember promising you that I wouldn't drink, smoke cigarettes, or get into things that could hurt me. I know there were promises I broke, and I take responsibility for that. I know saying "I'm sorry" doesn't undo those things, and I don't expect you to simply forget them.

But I want you to know that I did stop smoking. I kept that promise, and I'm proud that I was able to do that.

There were also little things I did that probably meant more to me than they should have. I changed my Discord password to something connected to you, and even changed my phone passcode to something connected to your birthday. I know those things might sound small, but they came from how deeply you had become a part of my life and my thoughts.

I'm not writing the actual passwords or passcodes here because this is a website that could be shared publicly. Those are private security details, but the meaning behind them is something I wanted you to know.

I don't want to make promises just because they sound good. If I ever get another chance, I want my actions to speak louder than my words.

I understand that my words may have lost some of their meaning because there were times when my actions didn't match them.

I regret that deeply.

If you ever gave me another chance, I wouldn't want to rebuild your trust with promises alone. I would want to earn it through consistency, honesty, patience, and my actions over time.

I know trust isn't something I can ask you to give me.

It's something I have to prove I deserve.

I still remember when you asked me what I trusted in, and I told you that I trusted in you.

I meant that.

Even after everything that happened between us, that answer still means something to me. You were someone I felt I could place my trust in, and that's something I never want to take for granted.

I know trust has to go both ways. If I ever get another chance, I want to become someone whose words you can trust just as much as I once trusted yours.

I don't want to change you.

And I don't want to change myself into someone I'm not just to make a relationship work.

What I want is to understand each other better.

I want us to be able to disagree without hurting each other. I want us to learn from what happened instead of repeating it. I want us to become better at loving each other when things aren't easy, not only when everything feels perfect.

And if you ever gave me another chance, I would genuinely try to improve myself—not by becoming someone else, but by becoming a better version of myself.

I would work on the things that hurt you, learn from my mistakes, and try to understand you instead of reacting the way I did before. I want to be true and honest with you, even when the truth is difficult, because you deserve honesty from me.

I don't want to make empty promises.

I want to show you through my actions that I mean what I'm saying.

I know you said we could be friends, and I respect that. I don't want to pressure you or make you feel like you owe me another chance.

But if I'm being completely honest with you, I still wish for one.

I wish we could try again—not to pretend nothing happened, not to erase the past, and not to go back to exactly what we were.

I want us to build something better from everything we learned.

Because despite all the arguments, misunderstandings, distance, broken promises, and pain, I don't look back at what we had and think it was a mistake.

It was real to me. You were real to me. And the love I felt for you was real.

Maybe that's why letting go has been so difficult.

There are still parts of me that remember you in the smallest things. Conversations, jokes, plans, little moments that probably meant nothing to anyone else but somehow became everything to me.

And if I have to beg you for another chance, I will. Not because I want to force you into loving me again, but because what we had means enough to me that I don't want to give up without being completely honest about how much I still want us.

I'd rather humble myself and ask you one more time than spend the rest of my life wondering whether I should have tried harder.

I know I can't decide what you feel. I can't ask you to forget the hurt or simply return to me because I still love you.

But I can tell you that if you ever decide there is another chance for us, I would take it seriously. I would want us to do things differently, communicate better, understand each other more, and protect what we have instead of letting disagreements destroy it.

I don't expect an answer immediately.

I don't want to force anything.

I just wanted you to know what my heart has been carrying.

Because if there is still a road that could lead us back to each other, I hope we find it together.

I still love you. I still care about you. And a part of me is still hoping that our story isn't finished yet.

♥
Made from the words that were never easy to say.
